deadlineLabel: Kaggle ARC Prize 2026 · ARC-AGI-3 closes Mon 2-Nov-2026, 23:59 UTC
base: Our best public score is Son's submission built on Daniel Franzen's public Milestone 2 notebook (full Flash-Next), with the border rule off, the animation feed and Son's tuned draft head. Every change below is judged against that notebook, not the older pruned line that fell to 8.14 and 3.93.

tracks.title: Model track
tracks.blurb: Make the model smaller and faster without losing play; learn from its own wins (RL / SFT).

tracks.title: Harness track
tracks.blurb: A few concrete harness changes aimed at the Kaggle score, each proven on repeat passes before it goes in.

sprints.goal: Know what actually moves the 28.94 notebook: a repeatable yardstick, the first RL round tested, the crash fixed.

model.title: RL round 0 on the new training regime's data (plan C)
model.done: Round-0 weights tested in play against the reference column on the RL page, held-out games included; we know whether it beats the model before training.
model.source: RL page: Round 0 training now; Son 5-Oct narrowed it to plan C data only

model.title: Faster / smaller model tested in competition shape before any submission
model.done: Any cut, quantised or draft-head change scores no worse than the full model on the same practice pass at equal time; otherwise it stays out.
model.source: Franzen-port post-mortem 2-Oct: the pruned 336g line passed every public-set test and still fell to 8.14 and 3.93 on Kaggle

model.title: Play-check the copycat games so RL can use them for the transfer test
model.done: The copycats Son wants for the transfer test are played by Son or the Boss and flipped to reviewed; held-out copies stay test-only.
model.source: datasets/copycat-games and recolor tier, all marked reviewed=false 4-Oct

harness.title: Repeat-pass yardstick on the 28.94 notebook
harness.done: The unchanged notebook run at least twice on the hard games at competition timing, with the run-to-run spread written down. No change is promoted on one pass.
harness.source: Our one-pass tests 1-4 Oct were all inside noise; public variance study: one run is a coarse screen

harness.title: Try Affectify's D' slot-priority cell on our notebook
harness.done: Our notebook with and without the D' cell, compared over repeat passes on the yardstick; kept only if it wins beyond the run-to-run spread.
harness.source: Son 5-Oct: Affectify D' scored 31.54 in one submission, inside the spread of Franzen's unchanged code; write-up docs/2026-10-05-dprime-slot-priority-vs-franzen.md

harness.title: Retry the token-count call instead of ending the game
harness.done: Checked whether the 28.94 notebook still ends a game after one 15 s token-count timeout; if so, a retry is added and a practice pass shows no game ended as crashed.
harness.source: 1-Oct practice: six of seven games killed by a one-minute server silence; 28-Sep sweep: 17 of 25 games lost the same way

harness.title: Finish the Jethro thinking-in-plain-English comparison and decide
harness.done: Enough passes of the forced-at-decode arm against Son's unchanged prompt to call it; kept only if it wins on repeat passes, otherwise dropped.
harness.source: Jethro chain f3, started 4-Oct; first one-pass result 3-Oct was inconclusive

harness.title: Rotated / mirrored level hint
harness.done: When a new level looks like the last one rotated or mirrored, the harness tells the model; tried on the yardstick against the unchanged notebook.
harness.source: Boss 4-Oct: Volume Control re-released rotated level by level, read as a private-set pattern

sprints.goal: Submit the first stacked gains on top of the 28.94 notebook.

model.title: RL round 1 if round 0 helped; otherwise switch to supervised fine-tuning on winning turns only
model.done: A trained model that beats the reference on held-out games, packaged as a Kaggle model the notebook can load.

model.title: Best faster build into the submission notebook
model.done: Practice pass at full competition timing finishes inside the time limit and scores at least the full model's yardstick.

harness.title: Stack the Sprint 1 winners into one notebook and submit
harness.done: One Kaggle submission carrying only changes that won on repeat passes; Boss told before it is pushed.

harness.title: Strategy check once a level has used a quarter of the game's time
harness.done: A stuck level triggers a short re-plan turn; tried on the yardstick, kept only if it wins.
harness.source: From one of the Milestone 2 public write-ups

harness.title: Carry notes from solved levels into the next level
harness.done: Tried on the yardstick; kept only if it wins. The 28-Sep level-clear reset arm (context dropped at each clear) gave no gain, so this keeps the history and adds the note.
harness.source: Milestone 2 public write-ups; our 28-Sep reset arm

sprints.goal: Last new ideas in; confirm the best combination on repeat passes.

model.title: Final model candidate chosen
model.done: One trained or faster model named as the final candidate, with its practice score next to the full model's on the same games.

harness.title: Combine model and harness winners; one or two submissions
harness.done: Each submission differs from the best by one known change, so a drop can be traced.

harness.title: Harness feature freeze at the end of the week
harness.done: No new harness ideas after Sun 25-Oct; only fixes.

sprints.goal: Freeze, pick the final two, make sure they finish in time.

model.title: Model frozen
model.done: Final weights fixed early in the week; no retraining after that.

harness.title: Pick the final two submissions
harness.done: One safe pick (best proven score) and one upside pick, both selected on Kaggle before the close, agreed by the Boss and Son.

harness.title: Time-limit and crash check on the final picks
harness.done: Both final notebooks have a clean full-timing run with no crashed games and room to spare on the clock.
